acetate is a major product of the metabolism of glycerol by halophilic Archae, but it is not a preferred carbon source for these organisms.

(1) acetate uptake and turnover in hypersaline brines are very slow; (2) acetate is not a preferred carbon source for halophilic Archaeal populations, and (3) acetate uptake by the natural community is limited by low affinity and not by V max.

“Acetate uptake by natural communities of halpphilic microorganisms in hypersaline ecosystems is characterized by low affinity for the substrate, which results in high acetate accumulation in the medium and in low turnover rates for the substrate.”
